components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      x-class-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.PostcodeValidation @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressValidation"
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            An optional honorific title for the pet owner. When present it must
            be one of MR, MRS, MS or DR. Used to compose the owner's
            'salutation' on the response.
          type: string
          pattern: "^(MR|MRS|MS|DR)$"
          example: 'DR'
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Flat form, kept for backward
            compatibility; prefer the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2'
            fields. An owner is valid when it supplies an address in either form
            (a non-blank 'addressLine1', or this flat 'address'). On the response
            this is the composed, normalized address: the normalized
            'addressLine1' with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2'
            appended when present, falling back to the flat value.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address
            (typically street number and name). Preferred over the flat
            'address' field when present; normalized the same way (upper-cased,
            whitespace collapsed, common street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal
            address (e.g. unit or apartment). Normalized the same way as
            'addressLine1' and, when present, appended to the composed 'address'
            after a single space.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must
            have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The normalized E.164 value is stored
            and returned (e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation"
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The postcode of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            exactly 4 digits and valid for the owner's city, whose region fixes
            the allowed range (Sydney/NSW 2000-2099, Melbourne/VIC 3000-3099,
            Brisbane/QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any
            4-digit postcode. Stored and returned unchanged when given.
          type: string
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. Once set it is stored and returned unchanged.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional. When present it is used to derive the owner's ageBand,
            computed against the registrationDate. Stored and returned unchanged.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Write-only hint, supplied on create, declaring that this owner
            deliberately lives in the same household as an existing owner (same
            last name and postcode). A second owner in an existing household is
            otherwise rejected as a household duplicate (409); setting this flag
            bypasses that duplicate block, so the owner is created as a declared
            household member and is not flagged as a possible duplicate. Not
            stored or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: >-
                The owner's salutation, composed as the title and the last name
                separated by a single space (e.g. 'DR Franklin'), or just the
                last name when no title is given.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Franklin'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,
                dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the country code,
                a space, then the national digits grouped in threes (e.g.
                '+61 412 345 678'). The raw 'telephone' field keeps the unformatted
                E.164 value.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                A stable code assigned when the owner is created, formatted
                '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where REGION is the region code derived from
                the postcode (or 'UNKNOWN' when no region can be derived) and
                HASH8 is the first 8 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over
                the normalized telephone concatenated with the last name. It
                carries no sequence number.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by all owners in the same household,
                i.e. with the same last name (compared case-insensitively with
                collapsed whitespace) and postcode. Formatted 'HH-<HEX12>' where
                HEX12 is the first 12 upper-case hex characters of SHA-256 over
                the normalized last name, a '|' separator and the postcode. It is
                deterministic, so owners with the same last name and postcode share
                it automatically.
              type: string
              example: 'HH-3A7F1C9B2E4D'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, shared the same first name and last name (compared
                case-insensitively). Assigned on create and returned unchanged.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-
                The fiscal year of the owner's business-day-adjusted
                registrationDate, formatted 'FY<YY>' where YY is the last two
                digits of the fiscal-year number. The fiscal year starts on 1
                July and is named for the calendar year in which it ends, so a
                registrationDate of 2026-08-01 yields 'FY27' and 2026-03-01
                yields 'FY26'.
              type: string
              example: 'FY27'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                A derived membership identifier formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate's fiscal
                year (see fiscalYear).
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M27'
              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented the `capacityWarning` flag, mirroring the existing `bulkSignupWarning` pattern (a create-time snapshot stored on the owner).

**Change:** `capacityWarning` is `true` when the owner's city already holds 40–49 owners at creation time (approaching the capacity limit of 50); the hard rejection at 50 (`CityAtCapacityException`) is unchanged.

Files modified:
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added the `capacityWarning` field (`capacity_warning` column) with getter/setter.
- **`service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`** — added `CAPACITY_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 40`, a `computeCapacityWarning(owner)` method (counts city members case-insensitively, excluding the owner being saved, and returns `count >= 40 && count < 50`), and wired it into the create branch of `saveOwner` right after the bulk-signup warning.
- **`mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** — added the `capacityWarning` mapping + `formatCapacityWarning` helper (null stored value → explicit `false`).
- **`resources/openapi.yml`** — added the read-only `capacityWarning` boolean to the owner schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it).
- **`resources/db/{h2,hsqldb,mysql,postgres}/schema.sql`** — added the `capacity_warning BOOLEAN` column.

The counting deliberately matches `assertCityHasCapacity` (same case-insensitive, exclude-self logic), so the warning band sits exactly below the hard limit. `AcceptanceTest.coreWarnsWhenApproachingCapacity` and the full suite pass (`BUILD SUCCESS`).
